items.title: U.S., Israel strike Isfahan and Tehran on Day 32 of Iran war

featured_image.name: Pakistan says it will host US-Iran talks after diplomats ... - AP News

items.description: As the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran entered its 32nd day on Tuesday, powerful explosions rocked both Tehran and the central city of Isfahan in what appeared to be some of the most intense aerial bombardments since hostilities began on February 28. The escalation came alongside fresh Iranian retaliatory strikes across the region and a parallel diplomatic push led by Pakistan to bring Washington and Tehran to the negotiating table.[1][2]

items.title: Trump tells allies to 'take' Strait of Hormuz themselves

featured_image.name: Trump criticizes allies who aren't helping secure the Strait of Hormuz

items.description:
President Donald Trump escalated his pressure on reluctant allies on Tuesday, posting on Truth Social that countries struggling with jet fuel shortages caused by Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz should either purchase American oil or seize control of the waterway themselves.

"All of those countries that can't get jet fuel because of the Strait of Hormuz, like the United Kingdom, which refused to get involved in the decapitation of Iran, I have a suggestion for you: Number 1, buy from the US, we have plenty, and Number 2, build up some delayed courage, go to the Strait, and just TAKE IT," Trump wrote, singling out nations that declined to join U.S. strikes against Iran. He added that the United States "won't be there to help you anymore" and that allies would need to learn "how to fight for yourself".[1][2][3]

items.title: Hegseth calls upcoming days 'decisive' in Iran war

featured_image.name: Iran War Live Updates: Pete Hegseth holds Pentagon briefing as Iran war intensifies

items.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday described the "upcoming days" as decisive in the month-long U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, pointing to widespread desertions within Tehran's armed forces and the degradation of its military capabilities as signs that the conflict is approaching a turning point.[1][2]

items.title: Gold climbs on report Trump may end Iran war

featured_image.name: Gold losses ease as Trump postpones Iran energy strikes - CNBC

items.description: Gold prices climbed on Monday after a Wall Street Journal report that President Donald Trump told aides he is willing to end the U.S. military campaign against Iran, even if the Strait of Hormuz remains largely closed. The gains extended into early Asian trading on Tuesday, with the metal also buoyed by Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell's comments at Harvard University that eased fears of an imminent interest rate hike.

items.title: Data centers warm nearby land by up to 16°F, Cambridge study finds

items.description: The sprawling data centers powering artificial intelligence are creating localized "heat islands" that raise surface temperatures by an average of 3.6 degrees Fahrenheit — and up to 16.4 degrees in extreme cases — affecting an estimated 340 million people worldwide, according to new research from the University of Cambridge.

items.title: Asian nations rush to buy Russian crude as Iran war chokes oil supply

featured_image.name: Russian oil arrives as Philippines battles 'energy emergency'

items.description:
A growing number of Asian countries are turning to Russia for crude oil as the U.S.-Israeli military conflict with Iran continues to choke off energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, triggering what the International Energy Agency has called the "largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market."[1][2]

The Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, and Sri Lanka have all signaled interest in purchasing Russian crude in recent weeks, joining established buyers China and India in a regional competition for barrels that analysts warn may soon outstrip what Moscow can deliver.[3][4]

items.title: Trump willing to end Iran war without reopening Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: White House: Reopening Strait of Hormuz Not Vital to Ending Iran War

items.description:
President Donald Trump has told aides he is willing to conclude the U.S. military campaign against Iran even if the Strait of Hormuz remains largely closed to commercial shipping, The Wall Street Journal reported on Monday, a move that could leave Tehran with lasting leverage over one of the world's most critical oil chokepoints.[1]

The shift signals a recalibration of American war aims as the conflict, dubbed Operation Epic Fury, enters its fifth week. In recent discussions, Trump and his advisers concluded that attempting to force the strait open would extend the fighting beyond his preferred four-to-six-week timeline, according to administration officials cited by the Journal. Instead, Washington plans to focus on its stated objectives — degrading Iran's naval and missile capabilities — while pursuing diplomatic channels to persuade Tehran to restore maritime traffic.[1]

items.title: US struck Isfahan ammo depot with bunker busters

featured_image.name: Iran War News: Massive Blasts In Iran's Isfahan After US-Israeli Strikes,  Trump Shares Video

items.description:
The United States struck a large ammunition depot in the Iranian city of Isfahan with a high volume of 2,000-pound penetrator munitions, according to a U.S. official cited by The Wall Street Journal. The strike triggered a chain of secondary explosions that lit up the night sky, with footage of towering fireballs circulating widely after President Trump shared an uncaptioned video of the attack on his Truth Social platform on Sunday evening. The Wall Street Journal confirmed the footage depicted the Isfahan operation.[1][2][3]

The strike is the latest in more than a month of sustained U.S.-Israeli military operations against Iran, launched on February 28 under what the Israel Defense Forces have termed "Operation Roaring Lion". Since then, more than 15,000 Iranian targets have been hit, according to the IDF, with the daily strike tempo declining from roughly 1,000 targets in the opening days to fewer than 100.[4][5][6]
